features.heading: Developer-first accessibility tooling
features.subheading: Go beyond rule-based linting. See how assistive technologies actually interpret your markup, and catch issues before they reach users.

0.title: Cross-Platform Simulation

1.title: Accessibility Audit Reports
1.description: Generate detailed audit reports aligned with WCAG guidance. Each report surfaces landmark issues, heading hierarchy problems, and missing accessible names with actionable remediation steps.

workflow.disclaimer: Speakable complements manual screen reader testing — it doesn't replace it. Use it to catch issues early and reduce the manual testing burden.

whyItMatters.heading: Why screen reader issues matter
whyItMatters.paragraph1: Screen reader usability issues are among the most common sources of accessibility failures on the web. These issues often go undetected until late in development — or until users report them.
whyItMatters.paragraph2: Manual screen reader testing is time-consuming and difficult to scale across large applications. Speakable helps teams identify these issues earlier in the development cycle, before they reach production.
whyItMatters.legal: With growing accessibility expectations under laws like the ADA, early detection isn't just good practice — it's risk mitigation.

challenge.label: The Challenge
challenge.title: Manual testing is a bottleneck.
challenge.description: Standard accessibility tools catch syntax, but miss user experience. Automated simulation bridges the gap between raw code and real human interaction.

cta.heading: Ready to improve your accessibility workflow?
cta.description: Catch screen reader issues early, prevent regressions, and build better experiences for assistive technology users.

usageGuide.title: Usage Guide
usageGuide.subtitle: Everything you need to analyze HTML accessibility with Speakable — from installation to CI/CD integration.

installation.heading: Installation
installation.description: Install as a project dependency for programmatic use and CI pipelines, or globally for CLI access anywhere.

cliCommands.heading: CLI Commands
cliCommands.description: The speakable binary accepts HTML file paths as arguments. All options are flags — no subcommands.

outputFormats.heading: Output Formats
outputFormats.description: Speakable supports four output formats, each suited to different workflows.

batch.title: Batch Processing
batch.description: Analyze multiple files in a single run. Batch mode continues processing even if individual files fail, and reports a summary at the end.

diff.title: Semantic Diff
diff.description: Compare before/after HTML to detect accessibility regressions. The diff identifies added, removed, and changed nodes with property-level detail (name, role, state, focus).

cicd.title: CI/CD Integration
cicd.description: Use exit codes and JSON output for automated pipeline checks. Exit 0 = success, exit 1 = user error, exit 2 = content issues or diff changes, exit 3 = system error.

webAnalyzer.heading: Web Analyzer
webAnalyzer.description: The web analyzer at /tool lets you paste HTML directly and see results instantly — no installation required.

steps.0: Paste your HTML into the textarea
steps.1: Select a screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, Narrator, or All)
steps.2: Optionally enter a CSS selector to focus on specific elements
steps.3: Click Analyze to see the predicted output

webAnalyzer.diffNote: Toggle diff mode to compare two HTML snippets side by side. Speakable will show you exactly which accessibility tree nodes were added, removed, or changed between the two versions.
webAnalyzer.voiceNote: After analyzing, click the 🔊 icon in the output toolbar to hear the results read aloud, or switch to line-by-line mode to navigate the output one announcement at a time using keyboard shortcuts.

voiceAnnouncer.heading: Voice Announcer
voiceAnnouncer.description: The web analyzer and browser extension include a built-in voice announcer that reads analysis output aloud using the browser's native SpeechSynthesis API.

playAll.title: Play All
playAll.description: Reads the entire output sequentially with pauses between lines and longer pauses between screen reader sections.

lineByLine.title: Line-by-Line Navigation
lineByLine.description: Mimics how screen reader users actually navigate: one element at a time.

voiceSpeed.title: Voice & Speed Controls
voiceSpeed.description: The voice dropdown includes a voice selector and a speed slider ranging from 0.5x to 2.0x.

0.title: Run in CI for regression detection
0.description: Add Speakable to your build pipeline so every PR is checked for accessibility changes.

1.title: Use selectors for component-level analysis
1.description: Focus on specific components with --selector rather than analyzing entire pages.

2.title: Check all four readers
2.description: Use -s all to see cross-platform differences. NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, and Narrator each have unique announcement patterns.

3.title: Save JSON baselines for snapshot testing
3.description: Store JSON output as baselines, then use --diff to detect changes between versions.

4.title: Start with audit reports
4.description: Use -f audit for a quick overview of accessibility health before diving into specific reader output.
